title: WIP trailer for my pizza deckbuilder, made using 99% AI code and 94% AI art (AI art is slowly being replaced but probably won't get to 0% by release). Would love any thoughts/feedback before I go live on Steam :D
author: stuffedcrust_studios
selftext:
My wife is an illustrator and she is gonna work thru replacing a lot of the AI art, also considering hiring a UI artist for the UI bits. I personally don't think the AI stuff looks too bad in general but there's a lot of negative sentiment around it and trying to market an indie game is already an uphill battle so just feels like gonna be better with less AI art (also human art does undeniably have more personality and character).

Anyway, would love any thoughts/feedback on the trailer and game in general.

Looking for playtesters so pls reply if you're interested and I'll send you a msg when I'm ready (soon!) with playtest build. It's a pizza themed deckbuilding roguelike.

The audio is human made as you can probably tell haha.

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body: If thats ai Art im impressed it Looks good

replies.author: stuffedcrust_studios
replies.body:
thanks!   
  
pretty much everything except the splash screen/title shot at the end is AI, with a lot of finessing, iterating + photoshopping to try and achieve some kind of cohesive result + aesthetic. the best art is still the human drawn art at the end tho i have to admit, am gonna try replace as much as i can before release but will almost certainly have some non-zero % of AI art in there still.

replies.author: brumiros
replies.body: What models did you use for the art generation?

replies.author: stuffedcrust_studios
replies.body: it's a mix, been in development 1.5yrs so models have evolved as i been working on it and been swapping and reworking things as better options were available. that said main ones are nano-banana-2 which did most of the characters and some of the UI and chatgpt imagegen v1 and v2 did most of the ingredient icons and a bunch of other bits.

comments.author: Laicbeias
comments.body:
Yeah is good. Some of the illustrations do the ai look. Its the highlights. The wiggle helps but yeah let your wife fix the characters. But rest looks.. coherent. Its in my opinion maybe the best ai based game ive seen. Its fun its creative. 

And you can get away with menu based gameplays. So you can use it where its the strongest.

And yes in game dev the most fun part always for me is doing your own audio. "I need a proper gras sqaush effect. Lets drop a very wet towel onto my plants"


Whats the gameplay like though? You pull card and get combos to finish a costumer who does negative stats?

Ofherwise good job

replies.author: stuffedcrust_studios
replies.body:
thanks, yeah am composer + sound designer by trade so will be doing the audio

gameplay is like you play ingredient cards to build a pizza and get the highest taste score, there's a bunch of mechanics like some ingredients buff adjacent meat, some can stack on others, some can be stacked on and get a bonus if certain types are on top/underneath, some add a bonus at turn start, some trigger if like 2 other mushrooms on the pizza etc etc, so a bunch of interlocking mechanics that make it a bit of a puzzle trying to work out how to maximise score, has a score x mult mechanic as well like Balatro.

then each turn you get more cards + energy but also the customer gets more hungry, and if hunger reaches the top you lose, so you need to balance taking one more turn to maximise pizza score with making sure their hunger doesn't get too high, then when you feed a pizza it adds score to satisfaction and removes from hunger, so you gotta fill satisfaction before hunger reaches the top.

some customers have abilities that affect your pizza (like one in the vid puts flies on it), then there's bases + sauces which apply bonuses or modify score for certain ingredients (eg bbq sauce buffs meat + spicy) and monsters have preferences which also adjust score (eg they hate herbs so herbs get -3 etc)

anyway if that sounds interesting to you lmk and i can put you on the list for a playtest if you like, very much looking for feedback at this point :)

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: The hunger-versus-score decision sounds like the real hook. For the first test, I’d ask players whether they can explain why they served now instead of risking another turn. If they can’t, that tradeoff probably needs surfacing before more card complexity gets layered in. I’m building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) for AI-built games and ongoing playtest loops; this feels like an ideal project to bring over when the build is ready.
